purpose: Risdiplam is used to treat spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), a genetic condition that weakens the muscles and makes it hard to move, breathe, and swallow. It is approved for people of all ages, from newborns to adults. It helps improve muscle strength and function in people living with SMA.
how_it_works: SMA is caused by a faulty gene that does not make enough of a protein called SMN, which muscles need to work properly. Risdiplam works by helping the body produce more of this important SMN protein from a backup gene called SMN2. By boosting SMN protein levels, the medication helps protect nerve and muscle function over time.
common_side_effects: Fever, diarrhea, rash, mouth sores or ulcers, joint pain, urinary tract infections, and runny nose are among the most commonly reported side effects. Some people may also experience nausea or upper respiratory infections. Side effects can vary depending on age and the stage of SMA.
warnings: Risdiplam may harm an unborn baby, so women of childbearing age should use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 month after the last dose. Men should also use contraception during treatment and for 4 months after stopping. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as risdiplam can interact with certain drugs. Do not stop taking this medication without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: Risdiplam is taken by mouth as a liquid once a day, with or after a meal. The dose depends on the patient's age and weight. For example, adults and children 2 years and older who weigh 20 kg or more typically take 5 mg once daily. Your doctor or pharmacist will calculate the right dose for you or your child. It comes with an oral syringe to make measuring the dose easier.
